items.title: Sumner Labat Interview, 1962-11-11
items.q: named Ward Pinkett but he died

ctx.x: What was it like up there in Virginia as far as music was concerned? Well, it was good. They had a brass band and they had an orchestra. And they had an orchestra, and I used to play second violin in the orchestra. And they had a professor from Richmond, Virginia to come up there and teach us twice a week, sometimes once a week. Well there were two of us who were playing violin in the orchestra at the time and the professor taking a light to me. And he said, boy I got music in you. And he started giving special…

There were some good musicians around in Virginia. I know that a lot of them, one fellow made a name for himself, went to New York, named Ward Pinkett but he died. I think he went to Hampton Institute. Yeah. I doubt if you'd known him, he's probably younger than you. We had an Italian professor up there, he was good. Professor Gadibasio was his name.

Gadibasio. Gadibasio was his name. And he was fun. We had a crack brass band up there. Oh yeah? Crack brass band up there. Readin'? Fakin'? Sure, I don't know fakin'. All readin'? You had to read all readin'. There was no fakin' in that. What about the brass band here?
